description: Composite figure of eleven panels mixing pseudo-in-situ SEM, EDS elemental mapping and two quantified-damage line plots. (a–a3) are SEM images of the same field at 0%, 0.7%, 5% and 9% engineering strain, each with a 20 µm scale bar and a "RD Loading direction" arrow; dark angular TiB2 particles sit in a lighter matrix. Red arrows mark fractured particles, already present in (a1), and one blue arrow in (a3) marks particle/matrix decohesion. (a4) plots "Number of cracks (cnt)" (0–160) against "Engineering Strain (%)" (0–16) for four series: TiB2 cracks number (FCC), TiB2 decohesion number (FCC), TiB2 cracks number (BCC), TiB2 decohesion number (BCC); all rise with strain, FCC cracking highest. (a5) plots the same four series as "Relative Frequency (%)" (0–50) versus strain. (b–b2) are multi-scale crack-path SEM images near the fracture surface (100, 20 and 5 µm scale bars, RD/TD axes), red arrows on TiB particle fracture, blue arrows on particle/matrix decohesion, black boxes linking successive magnifications. (c) is a fracture-surface SEM (10 µm) annotated Dimples, Void, Decohesion, Fracture, Primary TiB2, Eutectic TiB2, with (c1) its boxed region accompanied by EDS maps of Fe, Mn, Al, Ti and B. Together they show that tensile strain progressively fractures and debonds brittle TiB2 particles.

subfigures.description: SEM micrograph of the unstrained (0%) microstructure, 20 µm scale bar, showing numerous dark angular/blocky TiB2 particles dispersed in a lighter matrix; a horizontal arrow labelled 'RD Loading direction' points right.
SEM micrograph of the same field at 0.7% strain, 20 µm scale bar; a red arrow points to a defect-containing particle that has fractured.
SEM micrograph at 5% strain, 20 µm scale bar; two red arrows mark fractured TiB2 particles.
SEM micrograph at 9% strain, 20 µm scale bar; several red arrows mark fractured particles and a single blue arrow marks particle/matrix decohesion.

Line plot, x = Engineering Strain (%) 0–16, y = Number of cracks (cnt) 0–160, with four series: TiB2 cracks number (FCC) solid blue, TiB2 decohesion number (FCC) dashed blue, TiB2 cracks number (BCC) solid red, TiB2 decohesion number (BCC) dashed red; all increase monotonically with strain, with FCC cracking highest (from about 50 counts at 0% to over 100 at ~15%).

Line plot, x = Engineering Strain (%) 0–16, y = Relative Frequency (%) 0–50, with the same four series and legend entries as (a4); relative frequencies rise from roughly 15% (FCC cracks) and 9–10% (other series) toward ~32%, ~20%, ~17% and ~14% at the highest strain.

Low-magnification SEM of the crack region near the fracture surface, 100 µm scale bar, with 'Loading direction' arrow and RD/TD axes; blue arrows mark crack and void sites and a black box locates panel (b1).
Intermediate-magnification SEM (20 µm scale bar) of the boxed region of (b); red arrows mark particle fracture and blue arrows mark decohesion; a black box locates panel (b2).
High-magnification SEM (5 µm scale bar) showing closely spaced cracked TiB2 particles (red arrows) and particle/matrix interfacial decohesion (blue arrows) within a heavily damaged cluster.

SEM fracture-surface image (10 µm scale bar) with overlaid coloured annotations: 'Dimples' (yellow arrows), 'Void' (black arrow), 'Decohesion' (red arrows), 'Fracture' (blue arrows), 'Primary TiB2' (green arrows) and 'Eutectic TiB2' (orange arrows); a black box marks the region mapped in (c1).

Set of six panels: an SEM image of the boxed region plus five EDS elemental maps labelled Fe (red), Mn (green), Al (magenta), Ti (orange) and B (yellow-green); Ti and B are co-located on the blocky particles, Fe dominates the matrix, and Al/Mn show a more diffuse matrix distribution.

observations.observation: Panels (a), (a1), (a2) and (a3) are SEM images of the same microstructural field at increasing engineering strain (labelled 0%, 0.7%, 5%, 9%), each with a 20 µm scale bar.
Red arrows in (a1) and (a2) point to fractured TiB2 particles; in (a3) red arrows also mark fractured particles while a single blue arrow marks particle/matrix decohesion.

Panel (a4) has axes 'Number of cracks (cnt)' (0–160) versus 'Engineering Strain (%)' (0–16) and four legend entries: TiB2 cracks number (FCC), TiB2 decohesion number (FCC), TiB2 cracks number (BCC), TiB2 decohesion number (BCC).
Panel (a5) uses the same four series as (a4) but the y-axis is 'Relative Frequency (%)' on a 0–50 scale.
In both (a4) and (a5) every curve increases monotonically with engineering strain, and the TiB2 cracks number (FCC) curve lies above the other three series at all strains.
Panels (b), (b1) and (b2) form a multi-scale SEM sequence from 100 µm to 20 µm to 5 µm scale bars, with black boxes linking each magnification to the next.

Panel (c) labels, as printed on the image: 'Decohesion' (red arrows), 'Dimples' (yellow arrows), 'Fracture' (blue arrows), 'Void' (black arrow), 'Primary TiB2' (green arrows) and 'Eutectic TiB2' (orange arrows).
Panel (c1) contains EDS elemental maps annotated Fe (red), Mn (green), Al (magenta), Ti (orange) and B (yellow-green), showing Ti- and B-rich blocky particles in an Fe-rich matrix.
The caption states panels (a4) and (a5) are quantified damage mechanisms from SEM-EBSD analysis.

The caption states (b–b2) show crack propagation pathways near the fracture surface (multi-scale) highlighting TiB particle fracture, particle/matrix decohesion and cluster damage, and that (c, c1) show fracture-surface morphologies with ductile dimples, fractured TiB particles and interfacial decohesion.

The citing text states the first defect-containing particle fracture (red arrow in Fig. 8(a1)) occurred at true plastic strain εp = 0.0069 and applied true stress σa = 556 MPa, exceeding the yield stress σ0.2 = 503 MPa.
The citing text states the largest particles (>10 µm) constituted >80% of the volume fraction of TiB2, while smaller particles (0.8–5.0 µm) accounted for only 1.01% of the volume fraction.

The citing text states that both particle fracture and interface debonding occur during tensile straining and that the damage mechanisms from this figure were incorporated into a cohesive-element (COH3D8, bilinear traction-separation) model with a Weibull particle fracture strength.

unreadable_items: (a4) and (a5): individual data-point coordinates are not printed; values must be read approximately against the gridlines
(c1) EDS map intensity scales/colour bars are not shown, so element concentrations cannot be quantified from the maps
